Strong evidence in Alzheimer's trials; effects in healthy adults confirmed at 400–600mg.
600mg pre-workout increases peak power output. Effect is acute, not cumulative.

studies.title: Activity of Choline Alphoscerate on Adult-Onset Cognitive Dysfunctions: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
studies.population: adult-onset neurological disorders with cognitive impairment (cerebrovascular-associated)
studies.dose: not pooled/stated in abstract (7 RCTs + 1 cohort study)
studies.result: Alpha-GPC + donepezil improved cognition (MD 1.72, 95% CI 0.20–3.25), function (MD 0.79, 95% CI 0.34–1.23), behavior (MD -7.61, 95% CI -10.31 to -4.91); alpha-GPC alone also outperformed placebo/other medications (MD 3.50, 95% CI 0.36–6.63).

studies.title: Cognitive improvement in mild to moderate Alzheimer's dementia after treatment with the acetylcholine precursor choline alfoscerate (De Jesus Moreno, 2003)
studies.result: Significant improvement vs. placebo on ADAS-Cog, MMSE, GDS, ADAS-Total, CGI at 90 and 180 days; ADAS-Behav and GIS significant at 180 days. Placebo group worsened over the same period.

studies.title: Acute Alpha-Glycerylphosphorylcholine Supplementation Enhances Cognitive Performance in Healthy Men
studies.dose: 630mg (high dose) or 315mg (low dose) vs. placebo, single acute dose
studies.outcome: Stroop, N-Back, Flanker cognitive tests; growth hormone; physical performance (vertical jump, bench press throw, squat)
studies.result: Significant improvement in Stroop total score at both doses and faster Stroop completion time at high dose vs. placebo; no significant difference on Flanker or N-Back; no significant difference in physical performance or growth hormone between groups.

studies.title: The effect of 6 days of alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine on isometric strength (Bellar et al., 2015)
studies.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
studies.outcome: isometric mid-thigh pull peak force (lower body), upper-body isometric force
studies.result: Significantly greater lower-body isometric force change vs. placebo (98.8N vs -39.0N, p=0.044); upper-body force trended higher but was not statistically significant (p=0.127).

studies.title: Evaluation of the effects of two doses of alpha glycerylphosphorylcholine on physical and psychomotor performance
studies.journal: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
studies.design: RCT, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and caffeine-controlled
studies.outcome: countermovement jump (CMJ), isometric mid-thigh pull, upper-body isometric strength, psychomotor vigilance (PVT)
studies.result: No significant group differences for isometric strength (IMTP, UBIST) or PVT; 250mg group showed greater improvement in CMJ maximum velocity and mechanical power (p<0.05). 500mg group had significantly suppressed serum TSH.

studies.title: A comparative study of free plasma choline levels following intramuscular administration of L-alpha-glycerylphosphorylcholine and citicoline in normal volunteers
studies.journal: International Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, Therapy, and Toxicology
studies.dose: 1000mg IM alpha-GPC vs. 1000mg IM citicoline (single dose each, IM route — not representative of oral consumer dosing)
studies.result: Alpha-GPC produced a rapid rise in plasma choline (peak at 0.25–0.5h) that was considerably higher than citicoline's choline release over the same period.

verdicts.claim: Acetylcholine Synthesis — strong evidence, large magnitude, 9 studies
verdicts.reason: The pharmacokinetic comparison (PMID 1428296) confirms alpha-GPC raises plasma choline faster and higher than citicoline, and the Kerksick 2024 RCT measured cognitive effects at 60 minutes post-dose consistent with rapid absorption. Note the PK study used intramuscular, not oral, dosing, so the exact oral onset kinetics are not directly demonstrated.

verdicts.claim: Memory Encoding — strong evidence, moderate magnitude, 7 studies, 'effects in healthy adults confirmed at 400–600mg'
verdicts.reason: The strong evidence is in mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's patients at 1200mg/day (PMID 12637119), not healthy adults at 400-600mg. The one healthy-adult RCT at a comparable dose (630mg, PMID 39683633) showed a significant Stroop (executive/inhibition) effect but explicitly found no significant N-Back (working memory) or Flanker effect — 'memory encoding' specifically is not what improved in the healthy-adult trial.

verdicts.claim: Athletic Power Output — moderate evidence, moderate magnitude, 3 studies, '600mg pre-workout increases peak power output'
verdicts.reason: Findings across the three sports RCTs are inconsistent: Bellar 2015 (600mg x 6 days) found a lower-body isometric force gain but no significant upper-body effect; Marcus/Bellar 2017 found no significant strength (IMTP/UBIST) difference at 250mg or 500mg, only a CMJ velocity/power effect at 250mg; Kerksick 2024 found no significant difference in vertical jump, bench throw, or growth hormone at 630mg. None of the three used a single acute 'pre-workout' dose with a power-output outcome exactly as our copy implies — the 2024 trial is the most direct test of that scenario and found no physical-performance effect.

verdicts.claim: Neuroprotection — moderate evidence, moderate magnitude, 4 studies
verdicts.reason: The Sagaro 2023 meta-analysis and the De Jesus Moreno 2003 RCT both support a genuine cognitive/functional benefit of alpha-GPC in cerebrovascular and Alzheimer's-type dementia populations, consistent with the neuroprotective framing, though this is disease-population evidence rather than healthy-brain-aging evidence.

doseAssessment.trialRange: 250–630mg/day in healthy-adult/sports RCTs; 1200mg/day in the positive Alzheimer's RCT
doseAssessment.suggestedText: 300–600mg/day matches the sports/cognitive healthy-adult trials well, but is roughly half the 1200mg/day dose used in the clinical Alzheimer's trial our own 'Memory Encoding' claim leans on. Worth flagging that the strongest disease-population evidence used a substantially higher dose.

safetySignals.signal: Our copy cites 'a 2021 observational study' linking high-dose (>1200mg/day) alpha-GPC to cardiovascular/TMAO risk. This search did not locate that specific 2021 study; the closest identified evidence is a 2023 CARDIA prospective cohort study finding plasma choline (not alpha-GPC supplementation specifically) positively associated with incident CVD (HR 1.24 per SD), while a separate meta-analysis of dietary choline/betaine intake found no association with incident CVD. Neither study tests alpha-GPC supplementation directly, so the specific '2021 study, >1200mg/day' citation in our copy is unverified and should be re-sourced or removed.

gaps: The specific 2021 alpha-GPC/cardiovascular observational study cited in our copy was not located; only adjacent dietary-choline CVD literature was found.
No RCT was found testing a genuinely acute single pre-workout dose against a true power-output outcome — the three sports RCTs used 6-7 day loading protocols or found no physical-performance effect.
'Optimal cognitive effects at 4 weeks' has no directly matching trial duration in the retrieved set — sports RCTs ran 6-7 days, the Alzheimer's RCT ran 90-180 days.
